gap: No result ChatGPT got works out daily battery use from the makers' own figures. At Reolink's and eufy's shared rating of 300 seconds of recording a day, the eufy SoloCam S340 uses about 111 mAh a day (10,000 mAh ÷ about 90 days) and the Reolink Argus 4 Pro about 83 mAh a day (5,000 mAh ÷ about 60 days). The S340's bigger battery therefore covers about 30 more days without sun. Separately, TP-Link's own '45 minutes of sun per day' claim, multiplied by the 2.5 W maximum charging power it states, puts the Tapo C660 at no more than about 1.9 Wh a day at up to 100 events.
standout_why: I compared against the two pages ChatGPT cited, rottenwifi.com (best solar cameras 2026) and Reolink's 2026 solar buying guide. Rottenwifi gives 5,000 mAh and a 6 W panel for the Argus 4 Pro. For the S340 it gives no battery, panel or runtime figures, and for the C660 it gives nothing at all (it covers other Tapo models). Rottenwifi does not combine capacity with use or calculate any per-day or per-Wh figure; its own summary says it never gets to Wh or a daily energy balance. Reolink's guide gives 21.6 Wh for the Argus Eco Ultra and 5,000 mAh for the Argus 4 Pro, but it works out no sun hours or daily use either, and it contradicts itself on Altas sun hours (1 hour vs 5 hours). Neither page sets the cameras side by side at the same 300-seconds-a-day rating, and neither turns TP-Link's minutes-of-sun claim into a daily energy budget.
decides: This supports the S340 as the pick for shaded or snowy spots where the panel may get no sun for weeks. Its 10,000 mAh lasts about 90 days at the 300-seconds-a-day rating, against about 60 for the Argus 4 Pro. But the S340's removable panel is only 2.2 W, against the 6 W Reolink sells for the Argus 4 Pro, so the Argus is the better choice where there is sun to refill it. Two price points cut against the S340: eufy's own US store charges $219.99 today, not the $159.99 ChatGPT showed from Abt (I did not check the Abt price), and eufy sells the SoloCam E50, which it bills as the 'S340 Next-Gen', with a 5 W panel for $10 more ($229.99).
